text:
tess: Quick heads-up: I ran the onboarding sample with accelerated token TTL and saw a tight retry spiral after refresh. A bunch of 429s and duplicate create operations.

omar: Can you paste a minimal log snippet? Wondering if the SDK restarts its backoff state on auth success.

tess: Paste from local run:
```
12:03:10 outgoing id=onboard-7 auth=tok_old -> 401
12:03:10 onAuthRefresh started
12:03:10 onAuthRefresh done -> tok_new
12:03:10 SDK retried immediately (no jitter) -> upstream 429
12:03:10 retry counter reset -> retried again quickly -> duplicate resource created
```

lin: That pattern suggests the retry scheduler is being reconstructed when auth refresh completes. We should preserve RetryState so attempt_count and next_delay survive refresh.

omar: Agreed. Short-term fixes: 1) JS SDK parity change to keep retry state across onAuthRefresh; 2) add small randomized jitter on post-refresh immediate retry (suggest 25-200ms); 3) recommend Idempotency-Key in the sample onboarding flow.

tess: Also propose a tiny CI scenario that simulates mass token rotation (50-100 clients) and asserts duplicate count <1%. Will attach a repro script to the ticket.

lin: Implementation notes: in JS wrapper avoid new RetryState() on refresh resolution. Add a small helper 'postRefreshDelay = random(25,200)ms' before resuming the scheduler. Put the change behind a feature-flag for quick rollback.

omar: Good. Also add a lightweight telemetry ping (no PII) when a refresh happens within 1s of a retry and the upstream returns 429 so we can measure customer exposure.

ci-bot: CI queued: branch "devex/keep-retrystate-post-refresh" will run unit + integ in staging at 2026-09-01T02:00Z.

lin: I'll add the unit test asserting attempt_count/next_delay unchanged after fake onAuthRefresh.

tess: Filed INFR-9999 with logs, repro script, and the three proposed mitigations. P2 unless customers report incidents. Link: https://redwood-internal/issues/INFR-9999

omar: Thanks — after staging deploy let's run the 100-client overnight test and compare duplicate counts. If still high, we can add server-side idempotency guidance and consider a conservative refresh staggering in the sample wrapper.

tess: Will follow up with test results here. :pray:
